title: Best 22-Pint & 25-Pint Dehumidifiers (2026)
dek: The small-room size class, explained — and the compact dehumidifiers that keep a bedroom, office or laundry room comfortably dry.
description: The best 22-pint and 25-pint dehumidifier picks for bedrooms, offices and small rooms, sized under the 2019 DOE test, with ENERGY STAR and quiet options.
intro: A **22-pint or 25-pint dehumidifier** is the right tool for one damp room: a bedroom that feels clammy in July, a home office below grade, a laundry room where towels never quite dry. It's small enough to carry from room to room and cheap enough to run all summer, yet it pulls more water than you might expect from the number on the box.

That's because today's ratings come from the Department of Energy's 2019 test, run in cooler 65°F air. A modern 22-pint unit removes roughly what a 30- to 35-pint model did under the old labels, which is why so many shoppers end up buying more machine than they need. We compared models on DOE capacity, ENERGY STAR listings, humidistat controls, drainage and noise, and read owner reviews for reliability problems.
If you're still deciding between sizes, our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) walks through every tier.
topPicksLead: For most single rooms, the **Midea 22-Pint ENERGY STAR (MAD22C1AWS)** is the one to buy: efficient, easy to carry and right-sized for bedrooms, offices and laundry rooms.

blocks.text: Cooler test air holds less moisture, so the same machine earns a smaller number under the new rules. When you see a listing claiming 30 or 35 pints for a compact unit, check whether it's quoting the old standard. Our explainer on [how a dehumidifier works](/guides/how-does-a-dehumidifier-work/) covers why temperature changes the math.

We don't lab-test. We compare capacity under the 2019 DOE procedure, ENERGY STAR efficiency data, manufacturer manuals for humidistat range, drainage and auto-restart, and published noise ratings where available. Then we read owner reviews for recurring problems — leaky buckets, sensors that drift, compressors that fail after one season — and check the CPSC recall database.
For this size class we weighted efficiency and noise more heavily than raw capacity, because small units usually live in bedrooms and offices and run all summer.

sections.heading: What to look for in a 22- or 25-pint dehumidifier

items.label: A DOE 2019 rating
items.text: Make sure the pint figure is from the current test, or you can't compare models fairly.

items.label: ENERGY STAR certification
items.text: A small unit can run hundreds of hours a season, so efficiency adds up. See our [energy-efficient dehumidifier](/best/best-energy-efficient-dehumidifier/) picks.

items.label: A set-percentage humidistat
items.text: Dial in 45–50% and let the unit cycle off, rather than running on continuous.

items.label: Drainage you'll actually use
items.text: Small buckets fill fast. A gravity-hose port lets you skip the daily trip to the sink when the room is near a drain.

items.label: A quiet low setting
items.text: If it's going in a bedroom, look for a published decibel rating or a sleep mode. Our [quiet dehumidifier](/best/best-quiet-dehumidifier/) guide goes further.

blocks.text: For a single room, usually yes. The bigger question is how damp the space is, not just its square footage.

Search for this size and you'll run into plenty of familiar names. Frigidaire's FFAD2233W1 22-pint and its 25-pint models, GE's 20-, 22- and 25-pint portables, Whirlpool's 25-pint, Danby's 22-pint and the Comfort-Aire BHD-22A all target the same rooms as our picks. Several are older listings, so before you buy, confirm the unit is rated under the 2019 DOE test, check it isn't part of a past recall, and read recent owner reviews rather than ones from years ago.

blocks.title: Check for recalls
blocks.text: Millions of older small dehumidifiers from several brands have been recalled for fire risk over the years. Search the model number at CPSC.gov before buying used or older stock.

For most bedrooms, offices and laundry rooms, the **Midea MAD22C1AWS** is the 22-pint dehumidifier to buy: efficient, portable and right-sized. Choose the **Hisense 25-Pint** if your room runs damper, the **Midea Cube 20** if you want app control and a bigger reservoir, the **TCL TDW20E20** for a quiet bedroom, and the **Honeywell TP30AWKN** if you're genuinely between sizes.

faqs.a: The Midea MAD22C1AWS is our pick for most rooms: ENERGY STAR certified, rated at 22 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test, and easy to move. The Midea Cube 20 is the smart alternative with app control.

faqs.q: What's the difference between a 22-pint and a 25-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: About three pints a day of extra capacity. A 25-pint unit gives more headroom in a damp or slightly larger room, while a 22-pint is plenty for a typical bedroom or office. Both are single-room sizes.

faqs.q: Is a 22-pint dehumidifier enough for a basement?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most basements are larger and damper than a 22-pint unit can handle efficiently. Start at 35 pints for a small, moderately damp basement and 50 pints for a large or wet one.

faqs.q: Is the Frigidaire 22-pint dehumidifier any good?
faqs.a: Frigidaire's 22-pint FFAD2233W1 is a popular single-room model in the same class as our picks. If you're buying one, confirm it's new stock rated under the 2019 DOE test and read recent owner reviews; otherwise the Midea MAD22C1AWS is an easy alternative.

faqs.q: How much water does a 22-pint dehumidifier remove?
faqs.a: Up to about 22 pints, or 2.75 gallons, a day at the DOE test conditions of 65°F and 60% humidity. In warmer, damper rooms it can remove more; in cool, drier rooms, less.

faqs.q: Was a 22-pint dehumidifier called something else before?
faqs.a: Yes. Before the 2019 DOE test change, a unit like this would typically have been sold as a 30- or 35-pint dehumidifier. The machine didn't shrink; the test conditions got cooler.
